english_verification.review_scope: Checked current English Mod country/history/localisation, Z35 and B04 ideas, representative Z35 mission/event and formation passages, and exactly three fixed offline English Wiki pages/chunks. Mission reachability was not exhaustively audited.
unresolved: The native English idea references are authoritative for idea prose; all current mechanics remain bounded by the Mod scripts.
No exhaustive mission reachability audit was performed.

rationale.campaign_length: Z35 has 35 directly defined missions; B04's formation prerequisites, branching events, and later regional expansion substantially lengthen the campaign.
rationale.colonization: The dedicated mission tree has no overseas colonisation core loop; expansion toward the Deepwoods instead involves overland conquest and settlement.
rationale.complexity: Formation conditions, mission branches, Orcish labour, trade nodes, noble reforms, and religious events require simultaneous management.
rationale.dark_story: Missions and stories explicitly describe slave hunting, chained labour, plantations, wartime atrocities, exclusion of half-Orcs, and an optional Infernal Court.
rationale.difficulty: Strategic location, branching prerequisites, and expansive territorial goals require active warfare and resource investment before the economic strengths mature.
rationale.diplomacy: Negotiations over trade nodes, relations with neighbours, Griffon Lords, and Deepwoods allies shape possible routes, although diplomacy often supports expansion.
rationale.early_pressure: B04 must first settle in the designated region; after formation, Orcish labour, money, military points, and stability requirements constrain progression.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The Infernal Court, mage lights, and some supernatural storytelling appear, but knights, nobles, wine, and population institutions remain central to the missions.
rationale.narrative_density: Predecessor exile, settlement, enslavement, the old kingdom, the Deepwoods, and religious shifts form interwoven story arcs.
rationale.tall_play: Cities, palaces, vineyards, and provincial labour modifiers support construction, but the main mission arc ultimately requires broad expansion.
rationale.trade_economy: Wine production, trade share, and the conversion of enslaved people into trade goods form a distinct economic cycle.
rationale.warfare: Settling the Ashen Rose, hunting Orcs, expanding into the Deepwoods, and contesting the old kingdom's legacy all require sustained warfare.

identity.appearance: Rósande is formed after the Order of the Ashen Rose settles in Escann; its themes are Orcish labour, wine, noble knights, and Escanni expansion.
identity.formation_scope: The B04 branch in EscannFormables.txt changes the Tag to Z35 and swaps non-generic missions after settlement requirements are met; this is one continuous B04-to-Z35 chain.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and the ambition; excludes optional idea groups and racial or government bonuses. Candidate sets are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneous stacks.

description.text: The grape corvee does not merely refer to the practice of requiring the nobles to give up a portion of their slaves under a corvee system to work on royal lands every few months, but a complex legal and social system that codifies the idea that the Orcs are a uniquely inferior race, placed to serve their betters.

description.text: Shortly after the formation of Rósande, senior members of the Order of the Ashen Rose formed the Knights Rósande, the primary military elite of the country. Their crimson and black plate armour could be seen on the battlefields of Escann even far after it has stopped being used by other kingdoms, striking fear into Rósande's foes.

description.text: Led by the grim and cruel members of the Royal Slave Catchers, every free person (who can't afford a substitute) is expected to join with the slave hunting militias after a certain age. Here, they learn that the whips that lash the slaves also can be used on their backs, as speed outstrips all other consideration as they run down fleeing greenskins to drag them back to captivity.

description.text: The rolling lands that host Rosande make for excellent vineries, a fact latched onto by the recently settled Ashen Rose. With plentiful land, resources, and a cheap source of labor, it is often said that the true king of Rosande does not sit in the palace, but rather on the vine, and King Grape demands plenty from its subjects. No political decision is made in the country that the leadership doesn't turn to the bounty of its tressels.

description.text: The Order of the Ashen Rose was made up of lesser sons and bastards of the Lorentish upper class. With no future awaiting them in Lenecor they chose to carve a new future for themselves in Escann.

description.text: Many tales during the Age of Witch-Kings focus on a Rósander hero (a variant of the literary Romantic Hero), a dark and brooding gentleman-type who is often at odds with the world and its affairs - and most importantly an incredibly alluring figure for the fairer sex.

description.text: In July 1634 Surga's Rebellion shook the foundations of the kingdom. Almost one hundred orc slaves, in an unprecedented act, rose up under Surga, some even on horseback, and managed to kill almost sixty humans before being crushed. Reforms after led to even harsher laws, as well as demands from plantation owners and other free people for better equipped militias with more authority.

description.text: Our people are known to have more refined tastes than most, which has led to a booming trade in luxury goods in our lands.

description.text: Contrary to popular belief, not every Lorentish nobleman owns a vineyard, but it's common enough that we've gained a reputation for producing the best wine and building lavish palaces to showcase them.

description.text: Whereas knighthood generally carries some social benefits elsewhere in Cannor, nowhere is it as culturally exalted as it is in Lencenor, where knights are seen as both legends of the battlefield and heroes of verse and song.

description.text: Our courtiers are well learned in the arts of etiquette and diplomacy, able to carouse and cajole even the crabbiest of Corvurians. Let us employ them as diplomats and impress the courts of Cannor.

description.text: It is simply a fact of life that the various regional dishes of Lorent collectively comprise the finest cuisine in all of Cannor. The other nations recognize this, and bask in our culinary superiority.

description.text: Our courts aren't just for show: they are cultural and administrative marvels that balance pleasure with productivity. We can thus entertain more foreign ambassadors at once than most courts.

description.text: Although we may not have been at the head of the Lorentish host that seized final victory in the Lilac Wars, the decades-long conflict has had a great influence on our armies. Wherever the Lorentish martial salute can be seen, our enemies will know of our impending victory!

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you do not want slavery themes, long prerequisites, or frequent route branches.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Settle and form the country, roll an economy through Orcish labour and wine, then expand with knights, nobles, and old-kingdom inheritance.
player_overview.overview: Starting as the Order of the Ashen Rose, settle in Escann and connect knightly power, noble court, Orcish labour, and wine trade into one state machine. Rósande’s tree covers old-kingdom inheritance while exposing slavery, Deepwoods expansion, Half-Orc status, and the Infernal Court choice.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy dark narratives, cavalry warfare, noble politics, and high-pressure economic loops.
signature_features: Settlement by the Order of the Ashen Rose opens a longer kingdom mission line.
Orcish labour is tied directly to wine plantations.
Knightly nobles, Deepwoods expansion, and an Infernal Court branch run in parallel.
player_overview.tagline: Turn an exiled knightly order into Escann’s richest and most brutal rose kingdom.

reasons: The B04-to-Z35 predecessor and successor story remains continuous.
Orcish labour and wine change the rewards of expansion.
Knights, nobles, old kingdoms, and religious branches create a dense dark campaign.
warnings: Core missions explicitly support slavery and denial of personhood.
Settlement, resource gates, and branch prerequisites make the opening demanding.

positive_indicators: Cities, vineyards, and trade create material public prosperity.
Some routes turn slave goods into local production rather than continued export.
Social branches address Half-Orcs, Elves, and the Deepwoods.
values.rationale: Orc hunting, chain labour, slave labour, and converting slave goods into wine are direct scripted effects. Half-Orc events show weak recognition of marginalised persons. Wine, urban construction, trade prosperity, war, monarchy, religion, and unification do not independently determine this value score; optional branches do not erase the core slave system.
red_flags: Missions support Orc hunting, chain labour, and permanent labour modifiers.
Slave goods are systematically converted into wine production inputs.
Half-Orcs are excluded by both societies and lack a stable community.
